children: New cloud region is part of Microsoft's USD 20.5 billion India commitment
Microsoft has launched its India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad, positioning the facility as a strategic hub for cloud and artificial intelligence services across Asia and the Global South.

The launch comes as India prepares for a major expansion in data centre infrastructure. A Boston Consulting Group (BCG) study cited by Microsoft estimates that the country's data centre buildout could generate USD 140–200 billion in economic output through 2030.

The new region is Microsoft's fourth cloud region in India and will support Azure and AI services for enterprises. The company said additional services, including Microsoft Foundry, will be made available in the region.

The India South Central region features a three-zone architecture designed to support resilience and enterprise workloads. Microsoft said the facility would help organisations access cloud and AI infrastructure while supporting applicable data-residency and regulatory requirements.

Puneet Chandok, President of Microsoft India and South Asia, said the launch would strengthen India's role in the global digital economy. Microsoft's cloud regions in India are aligned with applicable MeitY guidelines and designed to support relevant requirements under the Digital Personal Data Protection framework, Reserve Bank of India regulations and CERT-In directions, the company said.

Microsoft added that customers would remain responsible for determining which regulatory requirements apply to their operations. Adani Group, Bajaj Finserv, HDFC Bank and PB Pay have signed up to use services associated with the new region.

The expansion forms part of Microsoft's USD 20.5 billion commitment to India. It also comes as the country seeks to expand its datacentre capacity to support growing demand for cloud computing, AI applications and digital services.
The BCG study estimates highlight the wider economic activity associated with investments in data centre construction, equipment, connectivity, power and operations.

India's expanding digital economy is expected to drive demand for infrastructure across the data centre value chain. This includes construction and engineering services, electrical equipment, cooling systems, networking infrastructure and technical workforce development.

Microsoft is also participating in the India-Southeast Asia (I-2SEA) subsea cable consortium, which is developing a 3,600-kilometre cable connecting India, Malaysia and Singapore. The cable will have dual landings at Machilipatnam and South Chennai and is expected to become operational in 2029.
The project intends to strengthen connectivity between India and Southeast Asian markets, supporting the movement of data and the development of cloud and AI workloads.
The new cloud region, connectivity investments and skills initiatives form part of Microsoft's broader effort to expand India's AI and cloud ecosystem.
